analysis.title: GS EUROPEAN EXPRESS: ASML | Argenx | Alstom | Carbonomics | Airtel Mobile Commerce Initiation | Macro | Global | Corporate Access
key_insights: ASML: after a Wilton site visit, GS cites five takeaways: strong High NA and ecosystem momentum, a deep competitive moat, multiple avenues for output optimisation, strong installed base management and upgrades business, and Match Act concerns overdone. Reiterates Buy (on Conviction List) with 83% upside.

Argenx: a MMN in Focus Event ahead of the December readout of empasiprubart's pivotal Phase 3 EMPASSION trial was incrementally reassuring. GS cites mitigation of grip strength variability (the primary endpoint), management confidence in Phase 2 ARDA translating to Phase 3, low drop-out rates and a strong C2 impact at the maintenance dose. Non-inferiority is the base case and superiority the bull case. Buy (on Conviction List) with 11% upside.

Alstom: after the 1H26/27 release, GS cuts year-end 27/28/29E group aEBIT post JV by 34%/6%/6% on weaker reported margins and lower JV earnings. Visibility on the backlog issues remains limited, though new disclosure of backlog by stage of project helps. Stakes in five JVs/associates now imply a combined value of EUR1.2-1.7bn, down from EUR1.4-2.1bn, excluding the loss-making ADEME JV. Sell.

Carbonomics: current emissions trajectory is more likely to see warming of 2.5-2.9C than the 1.5-2C target. GS sees stratospheric aerosol injection and marine cloud brightening as the most scalable and technically mature geo-engineering approaches. SAI has the strongest economic case at US$60-70bn a year per 1C of avoided warming, with aircraft operations the largest cost. MCB economics are more uncertain.

Airtel Mobile Commerce: GS initiates at Neutral with a 12-month price target of 260p, about 15% upside. It expects revenue ex-FX CAGR of about 26% over FY26-31E on rising penetration of Airtel Africa's subscriber base and growing ARPU. Risks are EM/FX volatility, competition from telco-backed peers and independent fintechs, and long-term margin pressure.

GOAL 2027 outlook: GS stays modestly pro-risk but favours more balance across and within assets as nominal and earnings growth approach a peak after the AI capex boom and the 2026 energy-driven inflation boost. Near-term risks are AI concerns, renewed energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and fiscal concerns. It favours selective growth alongside quality, defensive and high dividend/buyback stocks, and sees bonds as a better buffer against equity weakness.

GOAL: selective hedges against equity downside and energy/rate upside are attractive, as near-term rate and energy shocks could still challenge balanced portfolios. Higher starting yields improve prospective bond returns, and easing inflation should make equity/bond correlations more negative.

Germany 2027 outlook: GS estimates 2026 GDP growth of 1.0%, the strongest since 2022. It expects 0.1% qoq through the winter, 0.3% qoq from Q2, and 1.0% growth in 2027. Fiscal expansion adds an estimated 0.6pp to 2027 growth and the AI investment boom lifts export demand. Potential growth is capped at 0.5% by Chinese competition, elevated energy prices and retirements.
FOMC minutes: GS headline notes that 'almost all' participants judged that further action to raise the Fed funds rate would likely be appropriate.
US housing starts came in above consensus and building permits well below consensus. UK October headline inflation rose in line with consensus.

Rating changes: Airtel Mobile Commerce (AMCA.L) initiated at Neutral and Technip Energies (TE.PA) cut to Neutral from Buy on 18/11/2026. Oil services note: the LNG FID wave gets bigger, with GTT the preferred exposure.

PT changes of 10% or more: ABN Amro to EUR52.00 from EUR46.00 (+13.0%, Buy) and Worldline to EUR9.10 from EUR10.60 (-14.2%, Sell). EPS changes: Worldline -EUR2.87 vs -EUR3.34 old, Alstom -EUR2.19 vs -EUR1.13 old.

Other notable research headlines: Experian 1H'27 broadly in line with EPS ahead and a new $500m buyback; ZIM 3Q26 ahead of consensus with guidance raised; Ithaca Energy record EBITDAX and dividend upgrade to $560-580mn; British Land upgraded FY27 EPS guidance; TJX F3Q27 better than feared with FY comp outlook raised.

US and Asia headlines: Broadcom 3Q preview expects modest upside with focus on the AI revenue outlook and ASIC competition. Occidental takeaways from Houston keep Buy (on Conviction List). Tencent 3Q26 review sees an EPS reset with FCF pressure peaking. Europe tech note covers read-across from Nvidia's 3QFY27 results for European AI-indexed names.

sector_views.rationale: GOAL favours selective growth exposure alongside quality, defensive and high dividend/buyback stocks to balance Tech-heavy benchmarks. Opportunities broaden beyond AI capex beneficiaries to applications, adoption and productivity gains.
Technip Energies cut to Neutral while GTT is the preferred exposure as the LNG FID wave gets bigger.

earnings_insights: Alstom 1H26/27 (reported): GS cuts year-end 27/28/29E group aEBIT post JV by 34%/6%/6%. Reported margins were weaker than expected and JV earnings were lower than before the release. Alstom EPS estimate is now -EUR2.19 vs -EUR1.13 old, down 93.1%.
Worldline: GS EPS estimate is -EUR2.87 vs -EUR3.34 old (+14.1%), Sell.
Experian 1H'27 (reported): results broadly in line with EPS ahead, outlook adjusted, new $500m share buyback.
ZIM 3Q26 (reported): results ahead of consensus, guidance raised.
TJX F3Q27 (reported): better-than-feared 3Q as Marmaxx improves, FY comp outlook raised.
Ithaca Energy 3Q26 (reported): record EBITDAX and a second dividend upgrade to $560-580mn, with Rosebank first oil and Canada completion in 1H27.
British Land 1H26/27 (reported): strong leasing activity and upgraded FY27 EPS guidance.
Broadcom 3Q (upcoming, GS preview): GS expects modest upside, with focus on the AI revenue outlook, datacenter visibility and ASIC competition.
Tencent 3Q26 review: EPS reset, with FCF pressure peaking as new AI products scale.

Consumer weakness from inflation weighing on real incomes slows growth in winter, with momentum picking up from Q2.
The current emission trajectory is more likely to produce this warming than the 1.5-2C target, per the Carbonomics note.
Housing starts beat consensus while building permits were well below consensus.
Permits missed consensus by a wide margin.
